## Doctoral training

I have taught doctoral modules since 2009, including panel-data econometrics, spatial econometrics, discrete choice models and applied econometric methods for environmental and resource economics.

## PhD supervision

I have supervised or co-supervised **11 completed PhD theses**. Topics include forest economics, biodiversity conservation, environmental valuation, water, natural risks, protected areas, international trade and natural capital.

One PhD thesis was ongoing at the time of my 2026 CV.

## Research training

My involvement in training also includes Master’s theses, doctoral committees and support to early-career researchers. I aim to connect methodological rigour with real empirical questions and to expose students to reproducible and open-science practices whenever possible.
